selectedOriginals.caption: Manueline cloisters of the Jerónimos Monastery, Lisbon
selectedOriginals.inspection: 2007 original individually inspected: two-storey cloister with chamfered inner corners, broad lower arches subdivided by three slender shafts, two upper open arches under each broad bay, pierced round/lobed tracery and projecting piers. True open sky and continuous covered galleries; grass/paths and low fountain distinct. Figures/tourists excluded.

selectedOriginals.caption: The Jerónimos Monastery or Hieronymites Monastery / Lisbon , Portugal
selectedOriginals.sourceFamily: commons:the jerónimos monastery or hieronymites monastery.png
selectedOriginals.inspection: 2017 original individually inspected: pale limestone church, tall square bell tower with ribbed rounded dome/beaded finial and small corner pinnacles; south wall has giant narrow pointed windows and elaborate projecting central portal, pierced roof parapet and buttresses. Long integral west dormitory facade has lower open arcades, repeated upper round-headed windows, terracotta pitched roof and separate slender spired turret next to entrance. Foreground fountain/trees/city excluded.

additionalInspected.caption: The Jerónimos Monastery is a prominent landmark in Lisbon, Portugal and one of the most successful achievements of the Manueline style.
additionalInspected.inspection: 2009 local panorama copy actually inspected in full and four overlapping analysis crops. Local bytes are1920x401; Commons metadata describes12000x2510 original, which is not present locally. Eleven repeated normal facade bays counted each side of the central three-bay entrance pavilion; terminal turret-adjacent bays separate. Native plan supplies metric length. Fine carving is unresolved at this local resolution.

additionalInspected.caption: Main portal of Jerónimos Monastery, Lisboa, Portugal
additionalInspected.inspection: 2015 south portal original individually inspected: two actual dark door leaves under twin arches; broad shallow canopy arch with crossed ribs, dense tiers of sculptural niches/columns, large narrow pointed flanking windows, nautical rope relief, pierced fleur/foliate parapet, projecting buttress pinnacles and tall central statue/cross above. Preserve recognizable tiers/silhouette; no exact faces/inscriptions or copied image pixels.

additionalInspected.caption: Jerónimos Monastery (Mosteiro dos Jerónimos)
additionalInspected.artist: Jeremy Thompson from Los Angeles, California
additionalInspected.inspection: 2019 official visitor-sign photograph individually inspected: elevation diagram depicts long dormitory facade and church together, with separate museum/monastery entrances. Supports integral west wing inclusion while excluding detached modern halls; sign is not a measured architectural drawing. Do not reproduce sign text, logos or operating hours.

additionalInspected.caption: Claustro
additionalInspected.inspection: 2010 full cloister original individually inspected: actual chamfered corner bays, square court/diagonal dry paths, low circular fountain basin and separate grass panels. Lower broad bays have three slender posts and pierced spandrel/tracery; upper bays have paired arches under broad segmental arch. Parapet medallions and twisted conical pinnacles differ from church roof ornament.

additionalInspected.caption: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
additionalInspected.inspection: 2018 upper cloister original individually inspected: bell-tower dome is broad/ribbed, surrounded by tall corner pinnacles and crenellated/lobed base; nautical beaded finial/cross and clock below. Two slender spired turrets stand between cloister and dormitory; terracotta back church roof visible. Cloister chamfer, plainer rear church upper wall and patterned parapets constrain rear massing.

primarySources.review: Confirms Manueline identity and monastic foundation. Descriptive source; no measured plan/height.

Identifies Latin-cross church, projecting rectangular chancel, attached two-storey cloister, chapter house to east and refectory west. Describes west entrance versus elaborate south portal and major19th-century changes. Official gallery identifies the long west frontage as the dormitory/museum wing.

galleryPhotosInspected.scope: Whole official aerial actually inspected: integral long facade, west museum courtyard wings, church and roof arrangement; detached modern halls/planetarium distinguishable.
